Rheumatoid arthritis cannot be diagnosed by a blood test alone [d4, d8, d9]. Blood tests, such as those for rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-CCP antibodies, are important tools that can indicate RA and help confirm a diagnosis when combined with other factors [d1, d2, d5]. However, because these antibodies are not present in all RA patients and can occur in people without RA, a comprehensive evaluation including medical history, physical exam, and imaging is necessary for an accurate diagnosis [d4, d7, d10].
